name: Electret Microphone
purpose: Converts acoustic speech vibrations into low-amplitude millivolt-level electrical audio signals.
notes: The internal JFET inside the electret capsule requires steady DC bias power. A 10 µF series electrolytic capacitor isolates the DC bias voltage from subsequent amplifier inputs.
signalBefore: Acoustic speech pressure waves (300 Hz – 3.4 kHz audio)
signalAfter: Unamplified analog AC voltage (5–20 mV pk-pk riding on 0V DC)

name: LM741 Pre-Amplifier
purpose: Boosts weak millivolt microphone voltages up to standard line-level amplitude (~0.5 V – 1.0 V) for processing.
notes: Non-inverting or inverting op-amp topology. A 100 kΩ potentiometer in the feedback loop enables precise sensitivity calibration without saturating the op-amp rails.
signalBefore: Low-level AC microphone signal (5–20 mV pk-pk)
signalAfter: Line-level analog audio signal (~0.8 V pk-pk)

name: RC Active Bandpass Filter
purpose: Isolates the human speech intelligibility spectrum (300 Hz to 3.4 kHz) while eliminating low-frequency rumble and high-frequency noise.
keyParts: High-pass RC network (R1=4.7 kΩ, C1=0.1 µF)
Low-pass RC network (R2=4.7 kΩ, C2=0.01 µF)
notes: Prevents out-of-band harmonics from creating intermodulation distortion during subsequent AM modulation stages. Clean speech filtering improves receiver signal-to-noise ratio.
signalBefore: Wideband pre-amplified audio with background noise
signalAfter: Band-limited speech signal (300 Hz – 3.4 kHz band)

name: Buffer Amplifier
purpose: Provides unity-gain impedance isolation to prevent downstream stages from loading and de-tuning the RC filter network.
keyParts: LM741 or TL071 Op-Amp (Voltage Follower configuration)
notes: Connected directly after the RC filter. The extremely high input impedance preserves the filter's pole positions and Q-factor under varying dynamic loads.
signalBefore: Filtered speech signal from high-impedance RC filter
signalAfter: Identical speech waveform backed by low output impedance drive

name: Tone Control Circuit
purpose: Adjusts relative bass (low frequency) and treble (high frequency) frequency response for user acoustic clarity.
notes: Allows speech frequency shaping for hearing assistance, emphasizing high consonants (1.5 kHz – 3 kHz) for improved speech intelligibility in noisy environments.
signalAfter: Equalized audio waveform with tailored frequency response

name: AM Modulator
purpose: Modulates the amplitude of a high-frequency RF carrier wave or optical drive current proportionally with the incoming audio signal.
keyParts: High-frequency RF local oscillator / Crystal (455 kHz – 1.6 MHz)
Collector LC tank circuit / bias network
notes: Uses collector-amplitude modulation. The modulating audio varies the collector supply voltage or base-emitter current, producing an AM double-sideband with carrier (DSB-FC) waveform.
signalBefore: Low-frequency baseband audio voltage (0.8 V pk-pk)
signalAfter: High-frequency AM modulated RF envelope or modulated optical drive signal

name: Transmitter Output (RF Tx / Optical LED Tx)
purpose: Dual-transmission output stage driving either an electromagnetic antenna coil (RF link) or a high-flux infrared/optical emitter array (Optical link).
notes: Dual-output design allows instantaneous switching between non-line-of-sight RF propagation and noise-immune directed optical beam transmission.
signalBefore: Modulated AM carrier signal from BC547 modulator
signalAfter: Radiated electromagnetic waves (RF) OR intensity-modulated photons (Optical)

variants.name: RF Transmitter Driver
variants.notes: Radiates an AM electromagnetic wave testable with any standard AM pocket radio receiver. Tuned via ferrite rod inductor adjustment.

variants.name: Optical / IR LED Transmitter Driver
keyParts: High-output 940 nm IR LED array (e.g. TSAL6100)

typicalValues.label: Propagation Mode
typicalValues.value: Line-of-sight light beam (zero RF interference/EMI emissions)

variants.notes: Modulates LED brightness directly with the audio envelope. A black collimating tube extends operational optical distance significantly.

name: Receiver Front-End (RF Rx / Photodiode Rx)
purpose: Captures faint incoming airborne RF carrier signals or incoming modulated photon flux and converts them into an electrical AC signal.
notes: High sensitivity front-end featuring selectable tuned RF inductive capture or high-speed silicon PIN photodiode transimpedance conversion.
signalBefore: Airborne RF electromagnetic field OR modulated optical infrared light beam
signalAfter: Low-level received AM modulated electrical waveform (10–100 mV pk-pk)

variants.name: RF Receiver Front-End
keyParts: Ferrite rod antenna coil with secondary coupling tap
variants.notes: Parallel LC resonant tank selects the desired carrier frequency and rejects adjacent out-of-band signals.

variants.name: Optical / Photodiode Front-End
keyParts: BPW34 / PIN Silicon Photodiode (7.5 mm² active area)
variants.notes: Operates in reverse-biased photoconductive mode for maximum bandwidth and linear light-to-current response. The daylight blocking filter rejects artificial room lighting.

name: Envelope Detector & Demodulator
purpose: Rectifies the received AM carrier and filters out the high-frequency carrier component to recover the original baseband audio waveform.
keyParts: Germanium diode (1N34A / OA79) or Schottky diode (BAT85)
Demodulation low-pass filter (R=4.7 kΩ, C=10 nF)
notes: Germanium or Schottky diodes are critical due to their low forward turn-on voltage (0.2–0.3V vs 0.7V for silicon). The RC filter time constant is balanced to avoid diagonal clipping distortion.
signalAfter: Recovered analog speech audio waveform (100–300 mV pk-pk)

name: LM386 Audio Power Amplifier
purpose: Amplifies the recovered audio signal with sufficient current drive and power to drive an 8 Ω speaker or assistive headphone transducer.
keyParts: LM386 low-voltage audio power amplifier IC

typicalValues.label: Voltage Gain (Av)
typicalValues.value: 26 dB to 46 dB (20× default, up to 200× with 10 µF cap across pins 1-8)

notes: Includes an RC Zobel network on the output pin to suppress high-frequency parasitic ultrasonic oscillations and protect delicate hearing devices.
signalBefore: Weak recovered analog speech signal (~200 mV pk-pk)
signalAfter: High-current power-amplified audio signal (2.0 V – 5.0 V pk-pk into 8 Ω load)

name: Speaker & Assistive Headphones
purpose: Converts amplified electrical audio currents into clear, audible acoustic sound waves for the assistive listening user.
notes: The 3.5 mm audio jack automatically mutes the external speaker when headphones or hearing loops are plugged in, providing private assistive listening.
signalBefore: High-power electrical AC audio drive voltage
signalAfter: Clean, audible acoustic sound waves heard by the listener
